scope: Pronoun chain root-vs-rule isolation using unchanged production suffix rules

findings.evidence: All 22 kendi/herkes/siz/birbiri chain surfaces reject production morphology and accept with explicit test noun roots; 9 are also absent from flat-vocabulary protection. Existing downstream rules suffice for these surfaces.

şu exists as adjective; şunlar/şunlarda/şunlardakilerden reject both production and explicit-şu noun automata at şunl in isolated trace. şulardakilerden is accepted by both, showing regular noun inflection generates the n-less competitor. şunlar alone is flat-vocabulary protected.

findings.family: Foreign-looking competitor is in Turkish morphology inventory
findings.evidence: heroesinki accepted by production morphology; roots.tsv rows hero and heroes have noun class and frequency 30000. Do not attribute this observation solely to runtime English language switching.
findings.limit: Exact winning analysis/cost contribution not enumerated; appearance does not by itself prove these roots should be globally removed.

limits: Explicit noun root experiment is not a complete pronoun grammar implementation.
No production root modifications, ranking counterfactual, or new UI verification.
Surface restoration alone does not guarantee final decoder ranking after changes.
